findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. `board()` recognizes a Needs you item only when `team.needs_you` contains its ID, its stage says waiting for approval, or its next command contains `--resolve`. The current board producer sets `team.needs_you` to null (`src/forge/board_facts.py:224`). A normal unanswered review stop or worker question has a non-runnable resolve command (`src/forge/nextstep.py:773-784`), so it falls into Waiting or, after a day, Stuck. The pane therefore hides a decision the owner needs to make.
findings.title: Not done: Review stops and worker questions are missing from Needs you

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. For approval and stopped-review rows, a non-runnable `Next:` instruction becomes `next.command = null`; `next.line` is instead the first status sentence (`src/forge/nextstep.py:127-157`). This code presents that sentence after `→`, repeating the state rather than telling the owner how to act. Ready-to-merge rows never set `row.next` at all (lines 128-130), even when the board supplies a merge instruction. The supplied approval test masks the problem by inventing an actionable `next.line`.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The four-group and summary assertions import `summary.ts` directly here, so they pass even if the Board tab renders the groups or summary incorrectly. The mounted pane test checks only Moving and a refresh failure after a good snapshot (`src/forge/mod/hooks/pane.test.ts:48-71`); the first-timeout test checks only `/forge` text (`src/forge/mod/hooks/core.test.ts:175-195`). No test in the repository's pytest command mounts the pane for a complete grouped board or a failed first refresh, leaving both named Board-tab behaviors without entry-point proof.
